NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a steam-eductor-driven anode exhaust recirculation loop that activates only during the 400–650 °C thermal-transient window of start/stop cycles, maintaining a reducing atmosphere (pO₂ < 10⁻¹⁸ atm) at the Ni-YSZ anode without fresh fuel consumption. Standard practice uses inert-gas purge or simple fuel cutoff during shutdown, which still allows air ingress or re-oxidation as the stack cools through the critical 400–650 °C range where Ni→NiO kinetics are fastest. Adjacent-technique clearance: the closest existing practice is anode off-gas recirculation for fuel utilization (SOFC systems) or steam-jet eductors for vacuum priming (chemical plants); neither deploys recirculation as a dedicated, thermally gated redox shield. The departure is the ARRANGEMENT: a single catalog eductor on the exhaust line, driven by existing steam, that automatically establishes recirculation only when the stack temperature (measured by existing thermocouples) is between 650 °C (shutdown) / 400 °C (startup) and 400 °C (shutdown) / 650 °C (startup), creating a passive, zero-fuel redox buffer.

PHYSICS CHECK
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = oxygen partial pressure at anode during 400–650 °C thermal transients; the mechanism moves it DOWN by recirculating anode exhaust (H₂/H₂O/CO/CO₂ mixture, equilibrium pO₂ ≈ 10⁻²⁰ atm at 500 °C) via steam-eductor suction; this REDUCES the oxidation driving force (ΔG for Ni + ½O₂ → NiO) by >15 orders of magnitude versus air ingress (pO₂ = 0.21 atm). Magnitude verification: at 500 °C (773 K), Ni/NiO equilibrium pO₂ = exp(−ΔG°/RT) ≈ 10⁻²⁰ atm (ΔG° ≈ −180 kJ/mol). Recirculated anode gas at S/C = 2.5 gives pO₂ ≈ 10⁻¹⁸ atm (H₂/H₂O buffer). Air ingress gives pO₂ = 0.21 atm. The intervention suppresses the thermodynamic driving force for Ni oxidation by a factor of >10¹⁸, reducing NiO formation rate to negligible (parabolic rate constant kₚ ∝ pO₂ⁿ, n ≈ 0.5–1).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Standard practice bill for redox mitigation: (i) nitrogen purge system (bottles, regulator, solenoid valve, piping) — 4 catalog items + procedural sequence; (ii) or fuel-valve sequencing only (procedural). This intervention bill: 3 catalog parts (eductor, check valve, tee) + 2 procedural parameter changes on existing steam valve and PLC. Installation: all parts are standard pipe fittings welded/flanged into existing exhaust line (same trade, same schedule as standard purge piping). Commissioning: verify eductor suction at 5 bar motive (standard steam test). Operation: consumes 0.5–1.0 kg/h steam only during 2–4 h thermal transients per cycle (200 cycles × 3 h = 600 h over 5 years = 300–600 kg steam total, <0.1% of plant steam capacity). Maintenance: eductor and check valve are zero-maintenance catalog items (no moving parts in eductor; check valve standard 5-year inspection). No operational loss: recirculation occurs only during non-producing thermal transients (shutdown/startup); power generation window unchanged. Burden class: SAME as standard nitrogen purge (fewer consumables, same piping/instrument class, lower operating cost).

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Accelerated redox cycling on a single-cell test fixture (planar Ni-YSZ/YSZ/LSM, 10×10 cm active area) at 750 °C, 0.7 V, 0.5 A/cm² baseline. Two groups (n=5 each): (A) standard shutdown (fuel off, air ingress) / startup (fuel on); (B) eductor recirculation active 650→400 °C cool-down and 400→650 °C heat-up (steam 5 bar, eductor per bill). Cycle: 2 h at 750 °C → cool to 200 °C (4 h) → heat to 750 °C (3 h) → hold 2 h = 11 h/cycle. Target: 200 cycles (92 days). Instruments: existing cell voltage/current (power density), stack thermocouples (T), steam flow meter, post-test SEM/EDS (anode microstructure, Ni particle size), optical profilometry (electrolyte curvature → interfacial stress). Pass/fail thresholds: (1) Power density at 0.7 V after 200 cycles ≥ 0.35 W/cm² (group B) vs <0.30 W/cm² (group A, expected degradation). (2) Ni mean particle size increase ≤ 20% (group B) vs ≥ 2× (group A). (3) Electrolyte curvature change ≤ 5 μm (group B) vs ≥ 20 μm (group A). Kill criterion: any cell in group B cracks (voltage collapse to 0) or delaminates (impedance rise >50%) before 100 cycles → mechanism falsified. Duration: 92 days continuous.
